fields.meta_title: Movie Quiz: Play 8 Questions, Build Your Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Play an 8-question movie quiz with a source behind every answer, then build one for your own crowd on Emergent. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Movie Quiz Your Crowd Plays on Their Phones
fields.hero_description: Build a movie quiz that scores every team and keeps each answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Movie Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A movie quiz tests what a crowd remembers about films. Emergent builds the rounds and scoring, plus a table of every answer.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your film list

Name a decade, a director, or a list of films, and Emergent drafts multiple-choice questions on them, with wrong choices from the same era. Check each one and change it by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Rounds with their own scores

Split the quiz into rounds such as 1980s comedies or Best Picture winners. The results screen gives a score for each round, so players see which era they know and which they guessed.
fields.feature_3:
Team play on every phone in the room

Players pick a team on the first screen and answer one question per screen on their own phones. Emergent sets no cap on how many people play, whether that is 7 teams or a full lobby.
fields.feature_4:
Answers kept in a table you own

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player, the team, and the night. Sort by question to find the one nobody got, or by team to follow a season of Thursdays.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack message when the round closes

Set a closing time, and the app emails a reminder to anyone who has not finished. When the round closes, the host gets a Slack message with the final standings for each team.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, free to start

Use your venue's domain, included in Emergent and using credits. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Hosts Run a Movie Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
The $40 bar tab goes to the team on 9 of 10

Every Thursday, 7 teams at Harrow Street Taproom play a 10-question movie round on their phones. The app adds up each team's points after the last question and puts the leaderboard on the bar TV. Last week Back Row Crew finished on 9, ahead of Second Reel at 8, and took the tab.
fields.tab_content_2:
Question 7 trips 17 juniors on the opening shot

The 28 juniors in Fenwick Mill High's film studies elective take a 12-question quiz after each week's film. The app marks any question that more than half the class missed. This week 17 of 28 missed question 7, on the film's opening shot, so the teacher replays that scene first thing Monday.
fields.tab_content_3:
Noir night takes 23 votes after the final question

Before each monthly screening, Lantern Row Film Society sends its 64 members a 6-question quiz on the film's history. The last screen asks for a vote on the next theme night. This month 41 of 64 members played, and noir night took 23 of the 41 votes, ahead of musicals at 11.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every perfect score in the lobby earns a popcorn code

A QR code by the ticket counter at The Marquee on Fifth, a 2-screen independent cinema, opens a free 5-question quiz. Each entry lands in the cinema's own database. In the first month 312 people played, and the 74 who scored 5 of 5 got a popcorn code on the results screen.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Movie Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a movie quiz with fair questions, checked answers, and rounds that build from easy to hard.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Build each round around one thread, such as Best Picture winners, a single director, or 1980s comedies. A theme tells players what kind of recall the round asks for. Put the themes in your prompt, and Emergent drafts a round for each.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Confirm every answer against the film's credits or the awards record before the quiz goes live, and note where you checked it. A host who has to overturn an answer mid-round loses the room. Drop any question you cannot confirm in a minute.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write questions with one answer anyone can verify: a year, a director, a line, a number of awards. Skip questions on the best score or the scariest scene. A player who argues with an answer should find the record agrees with you.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Draw the wrong options from films of the same decade, cast, or director. A player should have to know the film, not spot the outlier. Keep all four options close in length and in the same form, four titles or four years.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each round with a question nearly everyone gets, and save the deep cuts for the end. Early points keep casual players in the game. On a 10-question round, aim for 3 easy, 4 medium, and 3 hard questions.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Play it once before the crowd does
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have two people take the quiz on their phones the day before: one film buff and one casual viewer. Watch for a question with two defensible answers and a round that runs long. Fix both, then share the link.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Look at what the room missed
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the round, sort the answers by question. A question nearly every team missed is either too obscure or worded badly. Rewrite it or replace it. Keep the questions that split the room, since those make the next round worth playing.

plan.angle: The top 10 is play-only: question lists, video rounds and quiz games (Land of Trivia, Collider, Sporcle-style categories, YouTube guess-the-film rounds), and none shows a host how to run a quiz for their own crowd. This page lets the searcher play an 8-question movie quiz on the page, each answer tied to a cited fact about a real film, then shows a bar trivia host, a film studies teacher, a film society and an independent cinema running their own quiz as an app that keeps every answer in a table they own.
tab_stories: Harrow Street Taproom runs a 10-question movie round for 7 teams every Thursday, the app totals each team's points after the last question and puts the leaderboard on the bar TV, and the Back Row Crew wins the $40 tab on 9 of 10.

The 28 juniors in Pinecrest High's film studies elective take a 12-question quiz after each week's film, and when 17 of 28 miss question 7 on the opening shot, the teacher replays that scene on Monday.

The Larchmont Film Society sends its 64 members a 6-question quiz before each monthly screening, the last screen is a vote on the next theme night, and 41 members play while noir night takes 23 of the 41 votes.

The Marquee on Fifth, a 2-screen independent cinema, puts a 5-question quiz behind a QR code in its lobby, 312 people play it in October, and the 74 who score 5 of 5 see a free popcorn code on the results screen.
